regressions.source: ProtocolUpgradeHandler._unfreeze: uint256[] memory ids = BRIDGE_HUB.getAllZKChainChainIDs(); for (uint256 i = 0; i < ids.length; ++i) {...} (dead here: the immutable hub is 0, artifact)
regressions.issue: The loop test now uses the decoded length _65 while the index check reads the stored copy of it at mem[u + ceil32(_1) + 160]; the store is written with ceil32(return_data.size) and the read with ceil32(_1) (_1 = return_data.size, no call between), so the two are not identified and the implied Panic(50) check comes back. The loop itself is dead code because of the immutables.
regressions.rule: Identify a saved return_data.size (_1) with return_data.size while no call intervenes, and forward a stored word to a later load of the same address; then the check i >= len under the test i < len is dropped.

new_findings.issue: The old P4 keys stor3[concat(mem[0])] now show the proposal hash (better), but the hash, already bound to _7, is re-expanded at every access, including two that read stor3[_7] before.
new_findings.rule: Reuse the variable bound to an expression for later equal expressions with no intervening write to their operands (here no memory write in [_5, u)).

improvements: P4 19 -> 5 (proposal keys resolved), P1 2 -> 0 (finding 3), P6 2 -> 0; storage fields read back from memory (mem[u + 26 len 6]) now print as their source uint48(stor3[..].field_0); unknown9c5392da's call shows the bytes length as a value.
notes: Diff 195 lines; all 4 changed functions read as per-function diffs.
summary: Keys and constants are better resolved; in executeEmergencyUpgrade's (dead) _unfreeze loop a stored length is no longer forwarded to its load, so an implied Panic(50) check returns (low), and the proposal hash is re-expanded instead of using _7.
